title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 205: The Cognitive Horizons of Deep-Space Missions
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 205 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Cognitive Horizons of Deep-Space Missions

Paragraph 1. Space agencies are planning to send astronauts to Mars in the future. On this trip, four to six astronauts will live together for almost three years inside a tiny home. Their living space will be about the size of a shipping container. Unlike astronauts near Earth who can talk to their team immediately, Mars astronauts will face a big problem. Radio messages will take up to twenty-two minutes to travel one way. Earth will look like a tiny blue dot in the dark sky.

Paragraph 2. To study how this lonely life affects the human brain, scientists use special places on Earth. One famous test place is Concordia Station in Antarctica, high up on the ice. During the nine-month polar winter, the weather outside drops below minus eighty degrees Celsius. Because of the terrible cold and dark, no airplanes can come to save people or bring them home. Everything looks white, and there is no sunlight for four months.

Paragraph 3. After three or four months alone in the cold, people start to change. Even strong astronauts find that their working memory becomes weaker, and they think more slowly. Brain tests show that the brain slows down to save energy when nothing changes around it. Also, small arguments about food, cleaning, and daily jobs begin to grow. Sometimes crew members get angry at the team on Earth instead of fighting with friends inside the small station.

Paragraph 4. Scientists are testing new tools to help keep astronauts happy and healthy. Watching ordinary movies or doing simple exercise does not fix the problem of living in a boring place. Instead, space teams are using virtual reality (VR) headsets. These headsets show pictures and sounds of green forests, ocean waves, and cool winds. Computer programs can also watch an astronaut's voice and face to spot stress early and suggest better sleep or softer room lights.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

Đoạn 4: "...pictures and sounds of green forests, ocean waves..."

q5.text: Mars astronauts can talk with Earth immediately without any delay.

steps: Đoạn 1: Tin nhắn radio mất tới 22 phút mỗi chiều, không thể nói chuyện tức thì.

q6.text: Airplanes can easily rescue people from Concordia Station during polar winter.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...no airplanes can come to save people or bring them home."

q7.text: Watching ordinary films completely solves the stress of boring space environments.

steps: Đoạn 4: "Watching ordinary movies... does not fix the problem..."

q8.text: Female astronauts handle Mars isolation better than male astronauts.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài không so sánh khả năng chịu đựng giữa phi hành gia nam và nữ.
